city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 61°F was the 23rd warmest November 13 high (tied) of 129 since 1891, the warmest since 2025.
text.p_yest: The high of 61°F was the 23rd warmest November 13 high (tied) of 129 since 1891, the warmest since 2025. The normal high for the date is 51°F, and the record is 69°F (1897, 2025). The low of 31°F was the 24th warmest November 13 low (tied) of 132 since 1888.
text.t_rec: Record highs keep coming. Record lows have nearly stopped.
text.p_rec: If Elko's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Elko has set 14 standing record lows, far fewer than the 75 that chance alone would give, and 116 record highs, far more than the 76 that chance alone would give. The 2020s hold the most record highs of any decade (52). Elko's all-time high is 107°F, on July 24, 1890.
text.t_chg: Elko's nights have warmed. Its days have warmed since 1986.
text.p_chg: Across 119 complete years: Elko's average low has risen +0.42°F per decade (95% range +0.32 to +0.53), about +5.5°F since 1895. Elko's average high shows no clear change: −0.00°F per decade, a range (−0.11 to +0.10) that includes zero. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1986, lows have risen +1.50°F per decade (95% range +1.13 to +1.86) and highs have risen +0.68°F per decade (95% range +0.17 to +1.19). The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 11 of 12 months. Highs rose in 1 of 12 months; November fell.

text.p_rain: Elko's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.09 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 10.0 inches a year. The wettest year was 1983 (18.34 in); the driest, 1919 (4.35 in).
